context: a letter from W. B. Tegetmeier, which you are answering
exchanges:
I have had the blocks cut as you desired and forward proofs. One I have returned to the engraver to have a little more shade cut away—

Would you have any objection to sign the enclosed   I should feel it a high honour to be recommended by you, in conjunction with my friend Mr Flowers.

If you would kindly return the paper this week it would be ready for the next meeting of the Council

I send you with this a number of the Field containing a rather graphic account of the habits etc of the Jungle fowl—

The suggestion that certain breeds are derived from the Sonnerattii are obviously incorrect and I consequently wrote a short reply in the paper of the following week.

Trusting you are enjoying good health | Believe me | Very truly Yours | W B Tegetmeier

C Darwin Esq

I have had much pleasure in signing the enclosed. No one has a better right to be a member of the Zoological Soc. than yourself. Many thanks for the blocks, which I think are greatly improved by being cut. When I receive the last I will write to Mr Murray about paying for the lot.

Many thanks for the Field: it is an interesting article, but contains nothing particularly new.— How hydra-headed the error is about the Gallus Sonneratii

My dear Sir | Yours sincerely | Ch. Darwin

Your note is dated 12th. but I only got this morning & I am very sorry that I quite forgot it was Friday, but you ought to receive this tomorrow, Saturday)
